description: Prompt text and suggestion-chip content for the induction terminal's Page 7 (Personal File + Personality) and Page 8 (In Your Own Words). Revised 2026-09-18 per design/induction-intake-audit.md §6: the three banal texture questions and bible §20's eight questions were replaced by a shorter set -- five open questions and a freeform box, down from eleven open questions -- with the surviving material folded into short one-line fields instead of being cut (old Q5 is now `likes`, old Q2 is now `good-at`). Every entry declares its own `bioPath`: the real sf2e Actor path its answer is written to, so nothing collected here is ever dropped on the floor (core/induction-bio.mjs consumes it). Every suggestion is illustrative only -- a quick-start a player may click to insert into their own answer, never a real answer for any of the six actual kids.
appearanceOptions: Never without their jacket, whatever the weather.
Looks like they just woke up, always.
Taller than they act like they are.
Dresses like someone twice their age.
You'd know them by their laugh before you'd know their face.

personalFile.purposeNote: Volunteers have no upper age limit — only conscripts do. Older than the cadets around you is a real, supported choice.

suggestions: Short, and tired of hearing about it
48 kg
61 kg
75 kg
The kit office weighed me twice and got two answers

personalFile.purposeNote: Nobody here is from here. How far off is entirely yours to decide.
suggestions: A fishing village four hours down the coast.
Two valleys over. You can see the smokestacks from the ridge.
A long way off. I'd rather not be specific.
Here, technically — but we left when I was small.

personality.text: The smallest thing that would make today a good day
personality.purposeNote: The cheapest, most reliable emotional lever in the campaign — your GM will actually use this.
suggestions: A letter from home, any length.
Getting through a whole drill without being singled out.
Someone laughing at something I said on purpose.
Hot water. Actually hot, not lukewarm.

personality.text: Something that reliably gets on your nerves
suggestions: People who talk through announcements.
Being told to calm down.
Wet boots.
Anyone who says "it's procedure" like that settles it.

personality.text: How you come across when someone first meets you
suggestions: Polite, and hard to read.
Loud, then embarrassed about it.
Watchful.
Friendly with everyone, close to nobody yet.

personality.text: Something you believe, and would argue about
suggestions: People are worth the trouble.
Rules are mostly for the people who wrote them.
If you can fix it, you should.
Nobody gets left in the water.

personality.text: What are you good at that has nothing to do with piloting?
personality.purposeNote: Competence outside the headline job is worth writing down — this is the one that most often turns into a side plot.
suggestions: Fixing things nobody else can figure out.
Making people laugh when they need it.
Cooking — really cooking, not just canteen trays.
Remembering names and faces. All of them.

openQuestions.text: Who's in your life? Friends, family, the people who would come if you called.
openQuestions.purposeNote: Write whatever you like here, at whatever length. Every name you give us is somebody your GM can bring back.
suggestions: My little sister. I write every week and she never writes back.
A friend back home who covered for me once and never brought it up again.
An old teacher who still thinks I'm going to be something.
Nobody yet. That's part of why I came.

openQuestions.text: And who would rather not see you again? A debt, a grudge, something you left badly.
openQuestions.purposeNote: Also open — as much or as little as you want. "Nobody" is a real answer.
suggestions: Someone I owe money to, who was decent about it, which is worse.
A brother I stopped speaking to. Neither of us can remember why.
Nobody's angry with me. I'd like to keep it that way.
A foreman who'll tell anyone who asks that I walked out mid-shift.

openQuestions.text: What were you part of before this — a school, a trade, a crew, a family business — and why did you leave it to come here?
openQuestions.purposeNote: You volunteered. Several hundred people did. This is where you say what you gave up to do it.
suggestions: My family's boatyard. Three generations, and I'm the one who left.
A school that quietly asked me to stop attending.
A dock crew. Good people, no future in it.
Nothing worth the name. That was the problem.

openQuestions.text: What would you rather the Directorate didn't know about you?
openQuestions.purposeNote: This one goes to your GM and stays there. It is not visible to the other players.
suggestions: Where I actually come from.
Why I really signed up.
Something I did before any of this.
Nothing at all. That bothers me more than it should.

openQuestions.text: A question for you, not your character: what do you want out of this? Is there something you have always wanted to do with a character and never got the chance to?
openQuestions.purposeNote: Say it plainly. This is the single most useful thing you can tell your GM, and it is the one place in this form where you are not in character.
suggestions: I want to play someone genuinely, unfashionably kind.
I've always wanted to be the one who talks the enemy down instead of shooting it.
A character who's bad at the thing everyone expects them to be good at.
Honestly? I want to find out how far the machine can be pushed.

freeform.text: Anything else. As much or as little as you like.
freeform.purposeNote: Nothing above has to have covered it. Write a paragraph, write a page, or leave it empty — all three are fine.
